nodes.summary: For a finite alphabet $T$, the encoded context-free grammar over $T$ whose start nonterminal is $S = 0$ and whose productions are $S \to \varepsilon$ and $S \to a S$ for every letter $a \in T$.
nodes.title: Grammar of all words

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an alphabet with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality. The predicate that holds of a pair $((g_1, g_2), w)$, where $g_1, g_2$ are encoded context-free grammars over $T$ and $w$ is a word over $T$, exactly when $w$ lies in the language of $g_1$, is a computable predicate.
nodes.title: Membership in the first grammar of a pair is computable

nodes.summary: There is an alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$, whether no word lies in both $L(G_1)$ and $L(G_2)$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.
nodes.title: Whether two context-free languages are disjoint is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is an alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for an encoded context-free grammar $G$ over $T$, whether $G$ is ambiguous, that is, whether some word has two different leftmost derivations from the start nonterminal of $G$.
nodes.title: Whether a context-free grammar is ambiguous is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$, whether $L(G_1) = L(G_2)$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.
nodes.title: Equivalence of context-free grammars is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$, whether $L(G_1) \subseteq L(G_2)$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of context-free languages is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is an alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for a pair $(G_1, G_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$, whether some word lies in both $L(G_1)$ and $L(G_2)$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$.
nodes.title: Whether two context-free languages intersect is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$, such that no multi-stack machine decides (in the sense of TM2-decidability), for an encoded context-free grammar $G$ over $T$, whether every word over $T$ lies in the language of $G$.
nodes.title: Whether a context-free grammar generates every word is undecidable

nodes.summary: There is an alphabet $T$, with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose languages are disjoint (no word lies in both) is not recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Disjointness of context-free languages is not recognizable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose languages are equal is not recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Equivalence of context-free grammars is not recognizable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ for which the language of $g_1$ is contained in the language of $g_2$ is not recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Inclusion of context-free languages is not recognizable

nodes.summary: The complement of PCP is not recognizable, over some finite alphabet.
nodes.title: The complement of PCP is not recognizable

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, such that the set of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose language contains every word over $T$ is not recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Universality of context-free grammars is not recognizable

nodes.summary: A recognizable undecidable predicate has an unrecognizable complement.
nodes.title: Post's theorem, contrapositive

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose languages are equal is co-recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Equivalence of context-free grammars is co-recognizable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, the set of pairs $(g_1, g_2)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ for which the language of $g_1$ is contained in the language of $g_2$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Inclusion of context-free languages is co-recognizable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with a primcodable encoding and decidable equality, the set of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ whose language contains every word over $T$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Universality of context-free grammars is co-recognizable

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive coding into the natural numbers and decidable equality. For an encoded context-free grammar $G$ over $T$, write $L(G)$ for the language it generates. The problem $\mathrm{OVERLAP}_{\mathrm{CFG}}$, the set of pairs $(G, H)$ of encoded context-free grammars over $T$ such that some word $w$ over $T$ lies in both $L(G)$ and $L(H)$, is recognizable by a multi-stack…
nodes.title: The overlap problem for context-free grammars is recognizable

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
